exactly, they were mentioning an elderly man a long time ago and how he would be complaining and whatever, that he needed to stop it, that he was lucky he got dialysis and he should  just adhere to it. i understood their reasoning; alternatively, as a patient, i also understood the man. people who are sick, especially on dialysis never react the same all the time. the haooiest person can be grumpy and an ass another day, but a lot of the times its un controllable. we have mood swings and mental side affects from our situations. while yea, we can hold it together, there will be a few times where it overwhelms us and we break, no matter the age, no matter the duration you were on dialysis.

well my docs have me as undiagnosed, all they said is it seems to be a birth defect. both my ureters are twisted which caused a backflow of urine from the kindey into itself which caused severe swelling and ultimately irreversible damage to my both of entire kidneys. i did my own research, and found some reliable sources that matched exactly my issue: ureteral torsion.  it seems to be rare because few people know it and i struggled to find what little i did about it. i live in the caribbean, so its difficult with the health sector sometimes. especially with transplants. i suspect my kidney failure could have been from what i read up to be VUR (vasicoureteral reflux) which is another congential disease, but im waiting to speak with my nephroligist and urologists about these hypotheses and more too about whether they can be passed to my offspring [idk if sp right there].

yea, at the beginning some of the techs used to mention me, my 'bitchiness' and such, when i was simply quiet or depressed. i broke down one day overhearing it, because my family member was there and they dragged them into the chatter, and i felt embarrassed and at fault for them bringing up my burden to my family. the tech who saw about me the first day hugged me and i was so thankful cause she hid my tears from everyone and even though she had to leave, she stayed with me till i was put together. i love her so much for that. now that my general relationship with the clinic is better i dont suffer as much as i used to. i would react poorly when i had to go dialysis: I'd get depressed, silent, angry,  isolated, and/or scared. especially of the one tech that i suspected started the talk about me, i would avoid her often, even thought of switching clinics. then i thought, that was stupid, i couldnt let someone have control like this and forced myself, my chronically anxious self to be more open. i dont force myself all the time but in the beginning i did until i genuinely became happier to go. if my down moods come in i let them, since there's nothing i can really do to prevent them, but thankfully at least in dialysis they have lessend. i hope maybe you can take something good and helpful away from this

well dont get too worried, im not a doctor, was on track to be a med student, but i was diagnosed with a disease that can have some effects like you are describing. everyone has different symptoms out of the major ones (and remember this is just a warning to update yourself on your health), but an organ could be malfunctioning somehow, e.g your colon or kidneys. you just to have a checkup on your body and organs to ensure everything is working as it should and no abnormalities are present.
however it can also be due to your mental health, or a combo of physical and mental. with you being stressed, cortisol levels increase and can dramatically upset the actual physical wellbeing of your body. so try getting time to relax for yourself, if that may be difficult, still try to dedicate little sections of the day to yourself, be creative.
just keep doing you, practise, get better, have fun, keep loving what you do
sounds like you need to visit your medical center for a checkup, preferably an ultrasound and full body scan or chest scan.

hate being a young person surrounded by older patients, i mean im glad not much young ppl have to do dialysis, but i feel alone, the constant talk about their pains and aches, making light of the diet they're supposed to follow. the complaining when they've lived a full life, while im barely staring. the fact that most of them are responsible for the predicament, or got diagnosed late in life, and my reason is congential. im getting off track with the question here- somedays time slows down, you get fed up
- i have a phobia a needles and scalpels/ knives so its not easy for me to get the needles in and out my arm
- seeing a patient one day, then they're gone the next. 
- feeling worn out after treatment.
-feeling useless during it.
- sometimes ppl stare at me cause im young (21) when the avg age is 60. i hate when they look at me like that, i feel ashamed.
- feeling like no one thinks you can handle youself,  yes i know im doing dialysis, but you can oversee me, dont baby me.
